title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is pure bookkeeping inside a long computation in the continuation of 'La Longue Marche'. The labels (182)–(196) and the cross-references (150, 151, 160, 172, 179, 180, 181; p. 639 (79); §49) all refer to earlier pages.

Setting (likely, not certain). The underlined objects appear to be (pro-)group objects over a base S_0/Σ_0 attached to a pair of special base points ρ, σ. A plausible reading is the two elliptic points of the moduli of elliptic curves, with automorphism orders 6 and 4, which would fit a finite group of order 12 (written O_12 or 𝔻_12). Under that reading:
- M_{ρ,σ} and its variant M^⇆_{ρ,σ} would be fundamental groups (or groupoids) with an extra twisting structure.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} would be their common quotient.
- N_ρ, N_σ would be normalisers and Z the centralisers of the local stabilisers.
- γ = γ_{ρ,σ} = O_12^* is a finite 'symmetry' quotient.

What the page states.
(190) is a morphism of extensions:
- top row: 1 → 𝔊^⇆ → M^⇆_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1;
- bottom row: 1 → 𝔊^+ → M_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1;
- the vertical maps are inclusions, and the identity on Γ.
- The brace notes that 𝔊^⇆ is identified with (an integral or completed version of) M.

(191) re-presents the same groups as extensions of the finite group O_12^*. The kernel is the product S N_ρ^? × S Z_σ^⇆ × 𝔊^⇆ (resp. × 𝔊^+). The quotients are O_12^* and O_12 = γ_{ρ,σ}, compared by the vertical arrow marked ⇓_×.

(192) is the analogous extension for Γ itself: 1 → S N_ρ^? × S Z_σ^⇆ → Γ_{ρ,σ} → O_12^× → 1.

(193) identifies the kernel factors:
- S N_ρ^? = μ_ρ ≅ {±1} (constant over S_0/Σ_0), from (172);
- S Z_σ^⇆ ≅ G_0, from (179).

(194) gives semi-direct ('1/2 directes') splittings, each by the finite group O_12^×:
- Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ O_12^× · G_0;
- G_{ρ,σ} ≅ O_12^× · 𝔊^+;
- G^⇆_{ρ,σ} ≅ O_12^× · M^⇆ (that is, · 𝔊^⇆);
- N_σ^⇆ ≅ O_12^× · G_0;
- N_ρ/μ_ρ ≅ O_12^*.
A first draft of (194), which used S N_σ instead of N_σ, is crossed out.

Purpose. These splittings feed the next page, (195): M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ ≅ O_12^* ⋉ (G_0 × 𝔊^+), etc. M itself is then recovered as a μ_ρ-covering pulled back from the extension 1 → μ_ρ → N_ρ → O_12^* → 1. In short, the aim is an explicit 'normal form' description of these anabelian groups as finite-group semidirect products, plus a μ_2-extension.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible, but the page relies entirely on statements proved elsewhere.

There is a notational wobble on the quotient finite group: O_12^*, O_12^× and plain O_12 all appear, joined by the arrow '⇓_×'. This suggests the bottom row of (191) should also read O_12^× (or O_12^*), or that a map between two forms of the group is intended.
The first version of (194) used S N_σ^⇆ and was crossed out; Grothendieck corrected it to N_σ^⇆ ≅ O_12^× · G_0, which is consistent with (192)–(193).

In (194), Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ O_12^× · G_0 and N_σ ≅ O_12^× · G_0 have the same shape. This is consistent only if Z_{ρ,σ} and N_σ coincide or are isomorphic. That may be intended, but it is not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Morphism of group extensions comparing a twisted/variant fundamental group M^⇆ with M over a common quotient Γ_{ρ,σ}.
ideas.modern_name: Morphism of extensions of profinite groups; outer Galois/Teichmüller-type quotient
ideas.where_published: The style is close to La Longue Marche (1981), unpublished but circulated.

ideas.what: Description of Γ_{ρ,σ} and M_{ρ,σ} as extensions of a finite group of order about 12 by μ_2 × G_0 (× 𝔊), with semidirect splittings by that finite group.
ideas.modern_name: Semidirect decomposition of normalisers/centralisers of finite stabiliser subgroups in anabelian fundamental groups of moduli stacks (elliptic points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous computations appear in work on profinite SL_2(Z) and π_1 of M_{1,1} (e.g. Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps); exact attribution unsure.
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the §49 material of La Longue Marche; unsure.

missed.claim: The surrounding pages (the next page in particular) set up the explicit structure of M_{ρ,σ} as a μ_ρ-covering of O_12^* ⋉ (G_0 × 𝔊^+). Grothendieck flags that the extension of O_12^* by μ_ρ should come from an extension of (μ×μ) via characters (ε_2, ε_3), but does not carry this out. This page only supplies the inputs.
missed.quote: Ces suites exactes se précisent, grâce aux décompositions 1/2 directes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Explicit normal forms for normalisers of torsion in profinite mapping-class-type groups are known in special cases. The thread lies on the next page, not this one.

deep.surprise_reason: This is internal bookkeeping (exact sequences and semidirect splittings citing earlier equations) inside a long computation. There is no new idea on the page itself, and the objects cannot be identified with certainty without the earlier pages.
transcription_corrections: The finite group written 'O_12' looks in the image like a D with a vertical bar (𝔻_12 / Ⓓ_12), consistent with the next page's '𝔻_12^*'.
In (193) the subscript of {±1} may be Σ_0 rather than S_0, as on the next page; '(172)' appears as '(172)' and the second reference as '(179)'.
'G_0' could be 'G_o' or a hatted G_a (compare the previous page, L_0 ≅ Ĝ_a); the glyph is ambiguous.
In (191) the vertical arrow on the right is '⇓' with a subscript ×; the bottom quotient is O_12 with an underbrace 'γ_{ρ,σ}'.
In the third line of (194), the object written after the semidirect product sign is M (with a superscript) encircled, with 𝔊^⇆ written underneath as an alternative name.
'id' in (194) is 'id.' (idem), placed above the reference column, meaning the same reference (150, 151).
The crossed-out line before (191) is 'et [des suites exactes]'; the crossed-out line before (193) reads roughly 'où on a [pour]'.
